**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

The operative grant is § 4(c) (p0021): a royalty-free, non-exclusive, **perpetual** licence to Contractor's Information incorporated into the Works, expressly **including the right to grant sublicences**, covering use, copy, modify, derivative versions and public performance/display "in connection with Company's business operations."

Why this clears the playbook:
- **Not revocable** — no discretionary revocation right for RadialSpark; perpetual term. Well clear of walk-away territory.
- **Affiliates/contractors** — not named, but the unqualified sublicence right lets us extend coverage to affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf without notice or consent, which exceeds the fallback (affiliates on written notice).
- **Transferability** — the grant is not styled non-transferable; § 10 (p0042) gates assignment of the Agreement on consent "which will not be unreasonably withheld," so a successor path exists.

Noted, not flagged (minor sub-elements short of preferred wording): the grant is not expressly "irrevocable," and there is no dedicated M&A/successor transfer carve-out. If the agreement is reopened for other reasons, adding "perpetual, irrevocable" and a successor-transfer permission in § 10 would be low-cost cleanup, but neither gap defeats the fallback position.
